# SPY Bankroll-Management Study (2005–2024, long-only)

*5,032 daily bars · every scheme invests the same **$1,200/year** into SPY · no shorting, no other tickers · the only differences are contribution timing and a 200-day trend rule.*

## The question

Can simple bankroll management beat just buying **$100 of SPY every month** — either by making more money, or (the real goal) by **cutting drawdowns** so the ride is survivable? Skipped contributions accumulate as dry powder and deploy when the rule allows. Idle cash earns 3%/yr in the de-risk schemes.

## Results — ranked by final value

| Scheme | Final value | Contributed | ROI | IRR | Max DD | Time in mkt | Buys | Sells |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| $300 quarterly | $98,858 | $24,000 | 311.9% | 12.5% | -39.6% | 100.0% | 80 | 0 |
| Baseline: $100/mo | $98,325 | $24,000 | 309.7% | 12.6% | -38.8% | 100.0% | 240 | 0 |
| $50 twice a month | $98,193 | $24,000 | 309.1% | 12.6% | -38.1% | 100.0% | 480 | 0 |
| Only buy > 200-SMA (accum) | $98,168 | $24,000 | 309.0% | 12.5% | -33.9% | 95.0% | 205 | 0 |
| Buy dips < 200-SMA (accum) | $95,827 | $24,000 | 299.3% | 12.3% | -38.8% | 91.7% | 70 | 0 |
| Trend system: in >200-SMA / out < | $76,857 | $24,000 | 220.2% | 10.5% | -17.2% | 76.0% | 243 | 59 |
| Partial de-risk: sell 50% < 200-SMA | $73,127 | $24,000 | 204.7% | 10.1% | -17.0% | 77.0% | 243 | 1007 |
| Trend system (200-EMA) | $64,006 | $24,000 | 166.7% | 9.0% | -23.2% | 79.8% | 269 | 80 |

*Reference — **Lump sum** (all $24,000 at the 2005 open, held): $170,985, max DD -55.2%.*

## What outperformed

- **Most money:** $300 quarterly — $98,858 vs baseline $98,325 (+$532).
- **Shallowest drawdown:** Partial de-risk: sell 50% < 200-SMA — max DD -17.0% vs baseline -38.8% (a 21.8% improvement).

**The tradeoff to notice:** the trend-exit schemes that dodge the 2008/2022 crashes cut the worst drawdown hard, but pay for it with cash drag and whipsaws — so they usually end with *less* money than just buying every month through the pain. Plain DCA is hard to beat on final value; where bankroll management earns its keep is **risk**, not return.
